free_tier.stated: Free accounts are capped at 10,000 stored contents — uploads past the cap fail with `error-limits`.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: The FAQ and API pages state no byte-size cap per file; the content-count limit is an object count. Absence of a size clause is not an unlimited claim.

retention.stated: Content is kept for 10 days of inactivity, and stays longer as long as it keeps being downloaded.
retention.notes: Free content is kept for 10 days of inactivity and longer while it is downloaded; past that period it may be moved to cold storage, from which importing requires Premium, and a guest/standard folder with an expiry is permanently deleted.

tooling: REST API at api.gofile.io (documented, CORS, per-endpoint rate limits); rclone backend 'gofile' (Tier 1) but its docs warn 'if you wish to connect rclone to Gofile you will need a premium account'; guest account creation is a single unauthenticated POST
chaining: Unlimited guest accounts created by API call (no email, no human-verification step) x 10,000 files each. Probe-verified; each guest account also brings its own 100 GB/30-day traffic bucket, so fetch load can be sharded by account.

limits.value: Content is kept for 10 days of inactivity, and stays longer as long as it keeps being downloaded.

limits_note: content is deleted after 10 days of inactivity unless it keeps being downloaded; past the storage period content may be moved to cold storage and importing it back requires Premium; most API endpoints (listing, direct links) return error-notPremium; 'Repeatedly exceeding rate limits may result in automatic IP bans'
reliability_note: 10-day inactivity expiry plus cold-storage migration makes it storage-with-a-TTL, not a drive; content-count cap (10k) bites hard on many-small-file datasets
confidence_note: the API page states the 10,000-content cap on a free account
